top5.title: Nvidia threatens to cut off clouds renting computing power to China
top5.description: Nvidia chip sellers would now refuse to supply neoclouds whose capacity is partly rented to Chinese companies. The BIS rule, which took effect on November 19, replaces a previous limit of 50% of GPUs.
top5.why: Nvidia’s reported move to restrict cloud providers serving China would significantly tighten the global AI-chip bottleneck and escalate U.S.-China technology controls.

top5.title: Dell reaches 22 billion dollars in revenue from AI servers
top5.description: Dell generated 22 billion dollars in AI server revenue, up 291%. Its order backlog has reached 132.3 billion dollars, which could delay some deliveries.
top5.why: Dell’s $22 billion in AI-server revenue and $132.3 billion backlog show that AI infrastructure demand is translating into unusually large enterprise orders, while also exposing supply constraints.

top5.title: Investigation finds undeclared AI use in 25 court cases
top5.description: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism found undeclared AI use in at least 25 cases in England and Wales. Some rulings included fabricated case law and nonexistent statutes.
top5.why: Undeclared AI-generated errors in at least 25 English and Welsh court cases highlight urgent risks for judicial integrity, professional accountability, and AI regulation.

top5.title: SAP reportedly considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs to pivot toward AI
top5.description: According to Bloomberg, SAP is preparing a plan covering at least 10,000 positions out of more than 110,000, particularly in product, engineering and sales. The company has not commented, and the figure could change after labor negotiations.
top5.why: SAP’s reported plan to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots toward AI could become a major signal of how generative AI is reshaping enterprise software workforces.

top5.title: Neuralink gets FDA approval to test its implant for ALS
top5.description: Neuralink has received FDA authorization to launch the pivotal LINK study, which will evaluate its brain implant in people severely disabled by ALS. U.S. adults with the disease can sign up for the patient registry.
top5.why: FDA authorization for Neuralink’s pivotal ALS study moves invasive brain-computer interfaces closer to potential clinical adoption and commercial-scale medical regulation.
